chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: We talked already about some of the differences between exchange traded funds,

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: mutual funds, and hedge funds.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: And those differences that we talked about are primarily having to do with how

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: they're traded and how visible what they're holding is to those who invest.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Another very, very important sort of difference is how are the managers

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: of these funds compensated?

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: In other words, there's some sort of rule for

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: each one that shows how the fund managers make money.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: And that's very, very important because the manner in which they're paid

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: incentivizes them to trade or act in certain ways.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: So let's talk about each one of these individually.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Before I get started though, I have to introduce one concept here.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: It's called assets under management, or AUM.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: And this is a buzzword that simply means how much money is being managed by the fund.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: It's important because for all of these,

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: part of the compensation is a percentage of the AUM.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: The managers of ETFs are compensated according to an expense ratio,

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: which is simply some percentage of AUM.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Expense ratios for ETFs are usually pretty low.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: They vary from as low as 0.01%, or 1 BIP as that might be called, to as high as 1%.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: But one that's up to 1% is fairly high and pretty unusual.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Mutual fund managers are also compensated using an expense ratio.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: These are somewhat higher than ETFs.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: They range from a low of typically about 0.5% to some that are very high up to 3%.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Now what's the reason for this difference?

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Well, mutual fund managers will tell you that the way they manage funds requires much more skill.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: They have much more discretion than those who are managing ETFs.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: ETFs usually are tied to an index.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: As an example, a popular ETF, SPY, is supposed to track the S&P 500.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: And all that an ETF manager has to do in that case is just make sure that they are holding all the stocks in the S&P 500.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Mutual funds, on the other hand, supposedly use more skill.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: And therefore, they can charge a higher expense ratio, both for the costs of their research and also for their skill.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Finally, hedge funds are a completely different breed in terms of how their managers are compensated.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: They follow an old model called 2 and 20, which means 2 or 2% of AUM plus 20% of the profits.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: So as you can see, it's higher than both of these other methods.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: And most importantly, it includes this component relating to profits, that 20%.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Now, one or two other things to clarify here.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: What I've been talking about is the way that the folks who manage these funds are compensated.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: Separately, if you are an investor in one of these funds, in other words,

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: if you give your money to one of these types of funds to be managed,

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: your return is based on how much the value of that fund increases.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: And in most cases, that increase is subject to what happens to the economy or what happens in the markets.

chunks.title: Incentives for fund managers
chunks.text: So let's look at a more detailed example of this 2 and 20 structure.
